masthead.name: Peter Petersen
masthead.about: I work in investment research and build the systems around it. I like difficult problems, learning what I need, and making the work useful to the person who has to use it next.

chapters.title: University of Oregon
narrative: By spring 2023, I had lost track of why I was at Oregon. I hit accounting courses I had little interest in. I spent more time in my fraternity and let school become secondary. My health and life outside class got away from me, and my family and people close to me had to help me pull out of it.
My grades fell that spring. They came back term by term before the Fisher internship.

At Fisher, I found that I cared about investment work and technology. I returned to Oregon and completed coursework in Python analytics, predictive modeling, supply chain operations, and business strategy. I graduated in June 2025.

chapters.title: Research Automation Consultant
chapters.summary: They asked me back in May 2026. In twelve weeks I built four workflows: one drafts quarter-end commentary, one generates short reports, one starts fundamental review paragraphs, and one briefs the top ten holdings. Working versions went in front of the analysts early, and their corrections went back into the builds.

systems.name: Quarter-end Commentary
systems.flow: 6 years of firm commentary · anonymized context library · first draft
systems.text: Parses six years of the firm's quarterly commentary and anonymizes every company, country, and sector reference. The anonymized sentences become drafting context, so each quarter's first draft comes out in the firm's structure and terminology. Analysts review every draft.

systems.name: Short Report Generator
systems.flow: ~100 published short reports · reusable forensic methods · sourced findings
systems.text: Built from roughly 100 published reports by Fuzzy Panda, Hindenburg, and Muddy Waters. Their recurring forensic methods became reusable components. A run applies only the methods relevant to the question, tests counterevidence, and delivers sourced findings, open questions, and next steps.

systems.name: Fundamental Review Paragraph Starter
systems.flow: daily screening list · comparison with last review · factual paragraph
systems.text: Starts from the day's screening list and compares each name's factor scores, performance, and valuation with its last review. When no recent review exists, the lookback expands to six months. Assembled in Python with no language model.

systems.name: Top Ten
systems.flow: SQL factor data + published research · one synopsis per holding · analyst review
systems.text: Pulls each top holding's factor data through SQL and pairs it with published research on the same company. Claude drafts the synopsis from that material, and every draft keeps its sources for analyst review.

artifacts.label: Reconstruction
artifacts.caption: Public sources and synthetic portfolio data. No client, portfolio, or proprietary firm information.

Kept sources with every output and folded analyst corrections into later builds; built with SQL, Python (pandas), and Claude skills.
